title: Student bank accounts: don’t be swayed by the freebies, freshers told
text:
In the scramble to sort out university accommodation, join freshers group chats and work out how a student loan payment is meant to stretch across a whole term, there is one big decision that is easy to put off but worth getting right: which student bank account to open.
Student accounts work like any other current account but come with two extras that don’t apply to the general public: an interest-free overdraft, and a lot of perks designed to hook you in as a customer for life.
However, while it is tempting to choose an account on the strength of the free cash, vouchers or other goodies, personal finance experts advise you not to be swayed by the extras.
“An interest-free overdraft could provide greater value over the course of a degree than a one-off freebie,” says Caitlyn Eastell at Moneyfactscompare.co.uk.
The ranking of the best student bank accounts for 2026-27 by the website Save the Student also places an emphasis on the size of the interest-free overdraft. “Maintenance loans now fall short of living costs by an average of £502 per month,” says Tom Allingham, the site’s student banking expert.
Its top picks for this year are the NatWest/Royal Bank of Scotland (RBS) student account, Nationwide FlexStudent and the Santander Edge student account.
To help you make your own mind up, here’s what’s on offer.
Santander Edge student current account
Freebies: a free four-year 16-25 Railcard, which is good for a third off most rail fares in Great Britain, as well as discounts on the tube when linked to an Oyster card. For students who travel home regularly, it is one of the more valuable perks on the market, potentially saving hundreds of pounds a year.
Interest-free overdraft: £1,500 in years one to three, but up to £2,000 in year five (if relevant).
Anything else? A prize draw: everyone who opens an account between 14 July and 16 October and makes a debit card purchase by the end of December is guaranteed at least £20, with one lucky student walking away with £100,000. Further prizes of £10,000, £1,000 and £100 are also on offer.
NatWest/RBS student account
Freebies: £100 cash, plus a four-year Tastecard subscription, which gets you money off at thousands of restaurants and cafes across the UK. NatWest says the Tastecard is worth £79.99 a year, although at the time of writing it was on sale for £39.99.
Interest-free overdraft: up to £2,000 from the second term of the first year (up to £500 available from day one), rising to up to £3,250 from year three onwards – one of the largest on the market.
Anything else? RBS is running an identical offer to NatWest for students in Scotland.
Nationwide FlexStudent
Freebies: £100 cash plus £120 in Just Eat vouchers, paid as £10 a month for a year. To unlock the offer, students need to pay in £500 and make five debit card payments by 11 December.
Interest-free overdraft: up to £1,000 in year one, up to £2,000 in year two and up to £3,000 in year three. (Your limit stays at £3,000 if your course is longer.)
Anything else? You could get a “Fairer Share” payment: each year since 2023, Nationwide has paid £100 to eligible members with a qualifying current account and savings or mortgage. Also, there are no fees for using the debit card abroad.
Lloyds/Bank of Scotland student account
Freebies: £100 to anyone who opens (or switches to) the account and pays in at least £500 by 30 October, plus up to £120 in Deliveroo vouchers – paid as £20 a month for six months to those making 20 or more debit card payments each month between November and April.
Interest-free overdraft: up to £1,500 in years one to three, rising to £2,000 for those studying on courses of four years or more.
Anything else? Both let you earn up to 15% cashback on everyday spending with selected retailers. Lloyds is also offering a prize draw in which five students will each win £9,790 – equivalent of a year’s maximum tuition fees in England.
HSBC Student bank account
Freebies: none at the time of writing.
Interest-free overdraft: up to £1,000 from day one, then up to £2,000 in year two, and up to £3,000 in year three.
Anything else? Access to HSBC’s 5% regular saver account, and to discounts via its home&Away offers programme.
Barclays Student Additions account
Freebies: none at the time of writing.
Interest-free overdraft: up to £500 from day one, rising to £1,000 in year one, and then up to £1,500 in year two and beyond.
Anything else? Not much to shout about this year.
TSB student bank account
Freebies: none at the time of writing, but the account pays a generous 5% (variable) interest on balances up to £500 – worth up to £25 a year.
Interest-free overdraft: up to £500 during the first six months, then up to £1,000 from months seven to nine, then up to £1,500 from month 10 onwards.
Anything else? Nothing of note.
Whichever account you choose, remember that the overdraft is not free money forever: once you graduate, most accounts convert into a graduate account that gradually withdraws the interest-free borrowing over a year or two, after which unpaid balances start accruing interest like any other loan.
